text.content:
Welcome to the Booth, producer. This module turns your table into Celmak's studio. Everything below is GM-only unless it says otherwise.

  1. Open the Producer Console: the broadcast tower button in the Token controls (left toolbar), the button on the ratings board, or the Producer Console macro in the Producer Macros compendium.
  2. Cast the contestants: Console → Ratings → Contestants…. Link each card to a player's actor, rename it, or hide companions who are sitting in the Box. Portraits default to the supplied chibi art.
  3. Go live: press Show board (or the ON AIR tab at the top of the screen). Every connected player now sees the ratings board.

Import the actors, items and tables you need from the The Hollow Garden: Season of Horrors compendium folder; the journal links open them directly.

The board shows two things:

  • Show Rating (1–5), the adventure's own ratings track. It starts at 3. Use the console's quick reasons (heroic sacrifice, betrayal, honeypot swallowed, off-script…) or the +/– buttons.
  • Fan meters (0–10) for every contestant. Portraits change with the fans' mood: crying at 3 or less, cool at 4–6, cheering at 7+. The leader wears the Fan Favourite crown; anyone at 2 or less is in the Danger Zone.

With Link fan meters to the Show Rating enabled (module settings), raising a contestant also nudges the Show Rating the same way.

Automatic rules

  • Rating hits 5: the studio erupts, a GM-only chat card offers Award Trinket to the highest-rated contestant (drawn from Celmak's Trinkets and added to the linked actor), and the rating resets to 3.
  • Rating hits 1: alarms, and a GM card lists Celmak's escalation options (Mood Gas vent, demon cast member, room reconfiguration, audience vote). The rating resets to 2.
  • At 2 and 4 you get a whispered reminder of Celmak's response.

Turn the automation off in module settings if you prefer to run the track by hand.

Celmak's schedule is fixed, but the audience doesn't need to know that. Games → Spin the Episode Wheel opens the rigging desk:

  • Tick which episodes are already done (they drop off the wheel).
  • Choose where the wheel will land. The default is the next episode on Celmak's schedule.
  • Pick a spin length and press Spin. Every client sees the same wheel slow down and land on your choice, with ticks, a drumroll and a fanfare.

When it lands you get a GM chat card with a link to the episode's journal page and a Roll title card button.

• Soundboard: each cue plays a sound for everyone and pops up a sticker of the host. Shift-click previews it only for you.
  • Stickers: pop any of the host's 28 stickers silently.
  • Celmak says: pick a persona (Host, Critic, Lover, Child), type a line or draw a random one, and it appears as a broadcast caption with the matching sticker.
  • Title cards: episode openers, Commercial Break (intermission; optionally −1 rating), Previously On…, and the Season Finale.
  • Effects: confetti, The Gap glitch, screen shake, and Mood Gas, which rolls the d6 table, fogs everyone's screen in the effect's colour and posts the DCs.

Each player can lower the module's sound volume, turn off stickers, or reduce motion in their own module settings.

Audience vote: enter a question and up to four options, then set the rigged percentages (or pick a winner and let the console invent believable numbers). Players watch a live vote with a countdown before the result is revealed.

Honeypot check: when someone reads one of the Garden's machines with Knowledge (engineering), open Games → Honeypot check. Roll from the linked actor's sheet or type in the total and the natural d20. The console sorts the result into the bands (61+ real answer; 60 or less with a natural 1–10 is an amusing fake, with a laugh and +1 rating; 11–20 is a detrimental fake) and whispers you the table result. Players only see what you tell them.
